data.one_liner: Flutter widgets that implement state management patterns using ValueNotifier.
data.what_it_does: Provides a set of widgets inspired by flutter_bloc such as ValueNotifierProvider, ValueNotifierBuilder, and ValueNotifierListener to make working with ValueNotifier cleaner and reduce boilerplate in state management.
use_when: You want to manage app state using standard ValueNotifiers with a bloc-like widget structure.
You want dependency injection for ValueNotifiers down the widget tree.
You want to separate presentation from business logic using ValueNotifier and builder/listener widgets.
avoid_when: You prefer a full-fledged state management framework like Riverpod or Bloc for complex asynchronous events.
You already use ValueListenableBuilder and do not need extra provider/listener wrapper widgets.
strengths: Familiar API for developers coming from flutter_bloc.
Reduces boilerplate when working with ValueNotifier compared to raw ValueListenableBuilder.
Lightweight and built directly on core Flutter foundations.
weaknesses: ValueNotifier can become cumbersome for complex multi-state logic compared to dedicated state management packages.
Relies on provider underneath for context lookups.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a general-purpose dependency injection and state management tool without wrapping ValueNotifiers specifically.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a more robust and formalized event-driven state management architecture.

alternatives.name: flutter_riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want compile-safe global state management without relying on widget context.
